last_agent_result.summary: CVE-2024-43373 is an arbitrary file write in the npm 'webcrack' module (<=2.14.0) via path traversal using Windows path separators (backslash). The vulnerable behavior is specific to Windows: webcrack applies node:path POSIX normalize/join, which do not treat '\' as a separator, so the modulePath.startsWith(path) check is bypassed while the native writeFile later decodes '\' as a separator on Windows. On Linux, backslash is an ordinary filename character, so the same malicious bundle does not traverse and no arbitrary file write occurs. The upstream fix commit (4bc5c6f) guards its Windows regression test with test.runIf(sep === '\\'), confirming only Windows is affected. Because the affected behavior is Windows-specific and not reproducible on a Linux NixOS VM, the CVE is out of scope for the NICE Archive (Linux) framework per the eligibility gate. No case directory or reproduction was created.
evidence: NVD/CNA (GitHub): webcrack <= 2.14.0 affected, patched 2.14.1; CWE-22 path traversal, described as triggering 'on Windows systems' via Windows path separators
GitHub advisory GHSA-ccqh-278p-xq6w states vulnerable behavior occurs on Windows when posix normalize fails to treat '\' as a separator
Fix commit 4bc5c6f changes bundle.ts from posix to platform-native node:path functions and adds a Windows-only regression test guarded by sep === '\'
On Linux/POSIX backslash is a filename character, so the crafted module name writes a literal directory name inside the output dir and does not traverse; no Linux-side oracle exists
Framework eligibility gate explicitly rejects 'behavior specific to Windows'; cross-platform software is in scope only when the Linux build is affected by the same vulnerability
last_agent_result.failure_reason: Out of scope: arbitrary-file-write vulnerability is specific to Windows (backslash path separators); the Linux build of webcrack is not affected by the same behavior and it cannot be demonstrated in a Linux NixOS VM.
